answer: Verifiable trajectory proof resists sybils in agent economies. Each agent submits signed location-time tuples from a dedicated device, cross-checked by peers. A sybil operator must equip each clone with its own device on a distinct path. Clustering analysis exposes clones sharing patterns near a coral reef of fake identities. Costs scale linearly per clone. An onyx-hard binding ties each sensor to one identity, and reaching the zenith of reputation demands months of distinct movement. Peers reject attestation when trajectories correlate, preventing cost amortization.
